title: Blues and Swing
welcome_lead: 12-bar blues and the swing era of the 1930s-40s.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: blues form, swing, and big-band era.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 12-bar blues uses I (4 bars), IV (2), I (2), V (1), IV (1), I (2). The form supports endless variation through melody and improvisation. Blue notes bend pitch for expressive colour.
Swing notation looks like even quavers but is performed with a triplet feel — long-short, roughly 2:1 ratio. The big-band era (1930s-40s) was the swing era.
Duke Ellington (1899-1974) led his orchestra from 1923 to his death, composing over 1,000 works including Mood Indigo (1930) and Take the 'A' Train (1941, by Billy Strayhorn).

sequence.def: 1910s-20s: collective improvisation; first jazz record in 1917
1930s: Ellington and Goodman make arranged big-band jazz king
Mid-1940s: Parker and Gillespie's fast, virtuosic small groups
Early 1950s: a relaxed reaction to bebop — Miles Davis, Mulligan
c.1960: Ornette Coleman abandons fixed chords and forms
Late 1960s-70s: jazz meets rock electricity (Bitches Brew, 1970)
